Name: Duration
Description: Controls how long the simulation runs. Longer durations produce stronger and more extensive crumbling effects.

Name: Strength
Description: Defines how intensely the rock or terrain breaks apart from the main body. Higher values result in more aggressive fragmentation.

Name: Coverage
Description: Sets how far the crumbling effect spreads inward from exposed edges, determining the affected area.

Name: Horizontal
Description: Biases the crumble effect towards flow origins or towards deposits, influencing the lateral direction of collapse.

Name: Vertical
Description: Biases the crumble effect towards higher or lower altitudes, controlling whether upper or lower terrain is more affected.

Name: Rock Hardness
Description: Controls material resistance, reducing how much terrain collapses. Higher values simulate harder, more resilient rock.

Name: Edge
Description: Expands or reduces the impact of crumbling specifically on sharp terrain edges, allowing for more pronounced or subdued edge effects.

Name: Downcutting
Description: Controls how deeply the simulation carves downward into the terrain during crumbling, affecting the vertical extent of collapse.

Name: Depth
Description: Adjusts the overall depth of the collapsed areas, determining how far the terrain sinks or breaks away.

Name: Direction
Description: Specifies the primary direction in which the crumbling effect propagates across the terrain.

Flubs.Name: X
Flubs.Description: Directs the crumbling effect along the X (horizontal) axis.

Flubs.Name: N
Flubs.Description: Directs the crumbling effect towards the north (upward in world space).

Flubs.Name: E
Flubs.Description: Directs the crumbling effect towards the east (right in world space).

Flubs.Name: S
Flubs.Description: Directs the crumbling effect towards the south (downward in world space).

Flubs.Name: W
Flubs.Description: Directs the crumbling effect towards the west (left in world space).
